results.content: 4. Active Learning and Human-in-the-Loop for NLP Annotation and Model Improvement. # Active Learning and Human-in-the-Loop for NLP Annotation and Model Improvement. ### A practical guide to using active learning and human-in-the-loop workflows for efficient NLP annotation, model training, and continuous improvement. They help us prioritize which data to label, involve human expertise at critical points, and continuously improve models in production. In this article, we’ll talk about what active learning is, how to implement a human-in-the-loop workflow for NLP annotation, and why this approach accelerates model improvement. In traditional machine learning, we would randomly label a big dataset and train a model, treating all those examples equally. In an active learning setup, we start with a small labeled dataset to train an initial model. In active learning, this usually means a person steps in to label the data points that the model isn’t sure about. A core question in active learning is: how does the model decide which examples to ask humans to label?

results.title: Human-in-the-Loop Machine Learning - Comet
results.content: > Annotation and active learning are the first step and cornerstones of the human-in-the-loop approach in AI/ML. Essentially, the data labeling process is simply an HITL process in which humans are involved in ML performance. Especially when data changes over time (which is very common), just adding some new labeled data can be much more effective than adapting an existing ML model to a new field. Increasingly, human resources know how to work with state-of-the-art ML algorithms but have no experience in choosing the proper interfaces to design quality and labeled training datasets. They employ many new ML/AI engineers but struggle to make their autonomous vehicle technology functional because they cannot scale their data annotation and labeling strategies. Labeling is a subject of study closely tied to Data Science and ML for researchers. Supervised learning models need more labeled data. Active learning is the process of choosing which data should be labeled. Just as no single algorithm, architecture, or parameter set will make an ML model more accurate in every situation, Nor is there a single strategy for active learning that will be optimal for all use cases and datasets. Regardless of the strategy, some amount of random data always needs to be disclosed and labeled to measure the accuracy of your model and compare your active learning strategies based on randomly selected items. In each iteration of active learning, a set of elements is defined and receives a new human-generated label, then the model is retrained with new data and the process is repeated. In the recent past, when researchers applied the well-known and extensive selection of data ImageNet datasets to ML models, they used 1,000 labels to identify the category of the image, such as *“taper,”* *“taxicab,”* *“swimming,”* and other primary classes. This can be difficult with Active Learning because as soon as you start labeling this data, it is no longer a *“different dataset;”* it becomes a set you know. You should use Active Learning in situations where you can provide data diversity with labeling and random sampling to only a tiny fraction of your data.

results.content: # 1 Introduction to human-in-the-loop machine learning. ### This chapter covers. * Annotating unlabeled data to create training, validation, and evaluation data. * Sampling the most important unlabeled data items (active learning). * Incorporating human–computer interaction principles into annotation. * Implementing transfer learning to take advantage of information in existing models. Unlike robots in the movies, most of today’s artificial intelligence (AI) cannot learn by itself; instead, it relies on intensive human feedback. Probably 90% of machine learning applications today are powered by supervised machine learning. This figure covers a wide range of use cases. An autonomous vehicle can drive you safely down the street because humans have spent thousands of hours telling it when its sensors are seeing a pedestrian, moving vehicle, lane marking, or other relevant object. Your in-home device knows what to do when you say “Turn up the volume” because humans have spent thousands of hours telling it how to interpret different commands. And your machine translation service can translate between languages because it has been trained on thousands (or maybe millions) of human-translated texts. ## 1.1 The basic principles of human-in-the-loop machine learning. ## 1.2 Introducing annotation. ### 1.2.1 Simple and more complicated annotation strategies. ### 1.2.2 Plugging the gap in data science knowledge. ### 1.2.3 Quality human annotation: Why is it hard? ## 1.3 Introducing active learning: Improving the speed and reducing the cost of training data. ### 1.3.1 Three broad active learning sampling strategies: Uncertainty, diversity, and random. ### 1.3.2 What is a random selection of evaluation data? ### 1.3.3 When to use active learning. ## 1.4 Machine learning and human–computer interaction. ### 1.4.1 User interfaces: How do you create training data?

results.title: Understanding Human-in-the-Loop Data Annotation and Labeling
results.content: # Understanding Human-in-the-Loop Data Annotation and Labeling. ## Introduction to Human-in-the-Loop Data Annotation and Labeling. Welcome to the dynamic world of Human-in-the-Loop data annotation and labeling, where human intelligence meets machine capabilities in perfect harmony. * By involving human annotators in data labeling tasks, machines can learn from high-quality labeled data, leading to more precise models. Moreover, human-in-the-loop annotation enables the handling of ambiguous or subjective data points that require human judgment, ultimately improving the overall robustness of machine learning models. ## The Process of Human-in-the-Loop Data Annotation and Labeling. Human-in-the-Loop data annotation and labeling involve a dynamic interaction between humans and machines to enhance the quality of training data for machine learning models. Next, human annotators review the data and apply relevant labels based on these guidelines. Human-in-the-loop annotation is an iterative process that leverages human intelligence alongside machine efficiency to continuously enhance the performance of AI systems. Navigating through the world of human-in-the-loop data annotation and labeling comes with its own set of challenges. One common hurdle is ensuring the quality and consistency of labeled data, as human annotators may introduce errors or biases. Variability in interpretations or labeling criteria among human labelers can lead to inconsistencies in the annotated data, affecting model accuracy. Innovations such as active learning techniques and semi-supervised approaches are being explored to address some of these challenges; however, overcoming these obstacles remains an ongoing endeavor for researchers and practitioners alike in the field of human-in-the-loop data annotation and labeling. * When it comes to human-in-the-loop data annotation and labeling, there are several best practices that can help ensure accuracy and efficiency in the process. ## Future Applications and Innovations in Human-in-the-Loop Data Annotation and Labeling. The future of Human-in-the-Loop data annotation and labeling holds exciting possibilities for the advancement of machine learning algorithms. In the fast-paced world of machine learning, Human-in-the-Loop data annotation and labeling play a pivotal role in enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of algorithms. As technology continues to evolve, so too will the methods and applications of data annotation and labeling. The future holds exciting potential for Human-in-the-Loop data annotation and labeling, with emerging technologies like active learning and semi-supervised approaches revolutionizing how we annotate data effectively.

results.title: Active Learning for Text Annotations, AI-Assisted Data Labelings
results.content: # What is active learning NLP and why it matters for AI-assisted data labeling, text annotation with active learning, and human-in-the-loop annotation. ## What is active learning NLP and why it matters for AI-assisted data labeling, text annotation with active learning, and human-in-the-loop annotation. When teams use **active learning for text annotation**, they empower annotators, engineers, product managers, and even domain experts to participate in a clearly defined loop: the model suggests the most informative samples, humans label them, and the model uses those labels to improve. For example, a retailer uses **interactive labeling with active learning** to classify product reviews across languages, while a healthcare provider uses **human-in-the-loop annotation** to ensure patient-privacy compliance and high-stakes accuracy. When you deploy **text annotation with active learning**, you bring together **active learning NLP** capabilities with **AI-assisted data labeling** and **interactive labeling with active learning**, all under a **human-in-the-loop annotation** framework.
